summary: The contract always supplies exactly two delivery counts and two recharge intervals; the closed form uses a fixed number of arithmetic operations and matches the unavoidable constant-time output decision.

optimality.argument: Any implementation must produce one integer answer for the fixed four-scalar contract, while three closed-form availability inversions, one LCM, and one maximum use a fixed number of operations.

replacement_checks.evidence: Producing the required integer decision for the fixed-arity delivery contract takes at least one operation, establishing Omega(1).
The accepted source evaluates three exact required-hour formulas and their maximum with no loop dependent on delivery magnitudes.
The dedicated regression compares against exhaustive legal scheduling on 3,136 small contracts and against monotone binary search on 100,000 deterministic full-range contracts.
